BRIEF_COLS.label: Who Meridian Is
BRIEF_COLS.text: Integrated health system and health plan operating Epic as core EHR, with a fragmented on-prem analytics estate (SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, SAS) and an outsourced analytics managed services provider consuming ~80% of delivery capacity on maintenance.

BRIEF_COLS.label: Where They Want to Go
BRIEF_COLS.text: Seven enterprise use cases are in scope: unified clinical + claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and automated close. AWS and Databricks are the target platform direction — not yet production-ready.

BRIEF_COLS.label: What Is Blocking Progress
BRIEF_COLS.text: No certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no AI audit trail evidence. Provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form. All seven use cases require evidence closure before value can be quantified.

BRIEF_COLS.label: What Nexus Can Do Now
BRIEF_COLS.text: Nexus has mapped the enterprise context across 19 dimensions and 146 evidence references. It can surface use case hypotheses, identify gap-to-decision chains, and prioritize evidence collection. It cannot yet produce decision-grade sourcing outputs or quantified value claims.

PRIORITIES.title: Close the lakehouse foundation evidence gap
PRIORITIES.detail: Epic Clarity, Claims, and Pharmacy data harmonization must be certified before the unified clinical + claims lakehouse use case can advance. AWS/Databricks medallion architecture is aspirational — not yet evidenced.

PRIORITIES.title: Establish formal data governance and semantic layer
PRIORITIES.detail: No certified semantic layer and no formal governance operating model exist. This blocks all seven use cases, particularly AI/LLM automation, where audit trail and data quality rule evidence are also absent.

PRIORITIES.title: Digitize provider contract terms and certify attribution
PRIORITIES.detail: Provider contract terms are not in governed digital form. Attribution ownership is unproven. Both gaps block cost transparency and provider quality use cases from reaching decision grade.

PRIORITIES.title: Govern contact center transcripts and certify intent taxonomy
PRIORITIES.detail: Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and member identity linkage are all unproven. Call center optimization cannot advance to agent-assist or next-best-action without these foundations.

PRIORITIES.title: Certify payment integrity model lineage and recovery workflows
PRIORITIES.detail: SAS-based payment integrity models lack governed lineage. Provider entity resolution is unproven. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not yet evidenced, preventing leakage quantification.

SIGNALS.quote: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse is promising, but strategy is not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no certified medallion architecture.
Governed data foundation for AI/LLM automation is promising, but not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no formal data governance.
Call center optimization is promising, but not decision-grade until contact center transcript evidence closes — transcript governance not yet evidenced.
End-to-end cost transparency is promising, but not decision-grade until Claims administration platform evidence closes — provider contract terms not digitized in governed form.

GAPS.title: No certified medallion architecture (AWS/Databricks)
GAPS.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse cannot advance. No bronze/silver/gold data products are evidenced. Target state is aspirational only.

GAPS.title: No formal data governance operating model
GAPS.blocks: AI/LLM automation use case is not decision-grade. Blocks semantic layer certification, AI audit trail, and data quality rule enforcement across all use cases.

GAPS.title: No certified semantic layer
GAPS.blocks: AI/LLM, cost transparency, and automated close use cases cannot produce governed outputs. SQL Server mart sprawl creates duplicated, ungoverned business rules.

GAPS.title: No patient/member identity spine loaded
GAPS.blocks: Unified lakehouse and call center optimization both require a resolved member identity. Claims, pharmacy, and EMR data cannot be joined without it.

GAPS.title: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form
GAPS.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases cannot produce margin or attribution outputs. Capitation and value-based contract logic remain in manual documents.

GAPS.title: Transcript governance and intent taxonomy not certified
GAPS.blocks: Call center optimization cannot advance to agent assist or next-best-action. Real-time CRM integration and member identity linkage are also unproven.

GAPS.title: Rules and model lineage not governed; provider entity resolution unproven
GAPS.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction cannot quantify recoveries. SAS model lineage is ungoverned. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not evidenced.

GAPS.title: Close workflow integration unproven; finance semantic layer not evidenced
GAPS.blocks: Automated close and reporting use case cannot advance. Manual reporting maintenance load and ungoverned metric definitions prevent close-cycle acceleration.

USE_CASES.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
USE_CASES.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Clinical Operations / Health Plan Operations
USE_CASES.value: Governed longitudinal patient/member view enabling population health, cost, and quality analytics. Value quantifiable only after EMR, claims, pharmacy, identity, medallion, and governance evidence are certified.
USE_CASES.gate: Epic Clarity medallion architecture + patient identity spine + claims/pharmacy harmonization + AWS/Databricks foundation
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CMO, and CDAO all cite this as the foundational strategic priority. It is the prerequisite platform for four of the other six use cases.

USE_CASES.name: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Automation
USE_CASES.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial
USE_CASES.value: Enables prior-auth, coding, and utilization management automation. Value quantifiable only after governance, semantic ownership, lineage, and control evidence are in place and workflow baselines are captured.
USE_CASES.gate: Formal data governance operating model + certified semantic layer + AI audit trail + data quality rules
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, Health Plan Ops, and Procurement all flag this as a top priority. It is the governance prerequisite for all AI/LLM use cases.

USE_CASES.name: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction
USE_CASES.fn: Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial / Analytics
USE_CASES.value: Reduces claims leakage through anomaly detection, FWA identification, and billing pattern analysis. Value quantifiable only after claims anomaly features, provider resolution, rules lineage, and recovery workflow evidence are governed.
USE_CASES.gate: SAS model lineage governance + provider entity resolution + investigation workflow evidence + recovery tracking
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CFO and Chief Experience Officer both flag payment integrity as a top strategic priority. SAS estate is the current detection platform but lacks governed lineage.

USE_CASES.name: End-to-End Cost Transparency
USE_CASES.fn: Finance and Actuarial / Health Plan Operations / Network Contracting
USE_CASES.value: Creates cost-of-care and margin visibility across claims, capitation, and provider contracts. Value quantifiable only after claims, capitation, contract, and GL reconciliation evidence is governed and finance/actuarial baseline is signed off.
USE_CASES.gate: Provider contract digitization + claims/GL calendar alignment + cost allocation rules + margin semantic model
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CDAO all cite cost transparency as a top priority. Provider contract terms not being in governed digital form is the single largest blocker.

USE_CASES.name: Call Center Optimization
USE_CASES.fn: Contact Center and Member Experience / Health Plan Operations
USE_CASES.value: Improves agent assist and next-best-action using transcripts, CRM cases, and claims status. Value quantifiable only after transcript, CRM, claims, intent, and QA-label evidence is governed and baseline AHT/containment/FCR data are loaded.
USE_CASES.gate: Transcript governance + real-time CRM integration + intent taxonomy certification + member identity linkage
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CIO all flag call center optimization. Chief Experience Officer owns member experience outcomes. Contact center platform and CRM are current-core but ungoverned for analytics.

rows.business_name: CFO / Finance & Value interview evidence
rows.context_item: CFO / Finance & Value says AI Benefits Realization Ledger needs FP&A validation and usage extracts required: The CFO would not let Tower count AI spend as delivered value until the usage extract, operational KPI movement, and FP&A validation all reconcile to the same program code. Copilot, ServiceNow, Workday, and developer productivity pilots can be measured, but Member Service AI Assist remains a candidate with no approved funding.

rows.business_name: Chief Experience Officer / Member Experience interview evidence
rows.context_item: Chief Experience Officer / Member Experience says Member Service Agent Assist Transformation needs Approved business case, baseline, and PHI controls required: No. Member Service AI Assist is a candidate/discovery opportunity. The funded work is the contact-center platform, knowledge foundation, data readiness, and AI governance controls. A separate Moves business case is required before AI Assist receives approved funding.

rows.business_name: CISO / Security interview evidence
rows.context_item: CISO / Security says AI Governance / Model Risk Controls needs HITL, audit logging, and model-risk evidence required: PHI access logging, human-in-the-loop validation, prompt/audit trails, and model inventory ownership must be complete before service, Workday, or member-facing AI pilots scale beyond controlled pilots.

rows.business_name: Contact Center / Member Service Operations interview evidence
rows.context_item: Contact Center / Member Service Operations says Contact Center Platform / Knowledge Modernization needs AHT, FCR, transfer, CSAT, and QA baselines required: Operations needs call reason, AHT, FCR, transfer, knowledge-search, QA, and escalation baselines before AI Assist is funded. Usage data from Genesys and the knowledge platform should prove the foundation first.

rows.business_name: CIO / Enterprise Technology interview evidence
rows.context_item: CIO / Enterprise Technology says FY26 AI spend governance needs Budget, program, and benefits ledger ties required: The CIO should show AI spend as tagged inside approved platforms and programs: Copilot, ServiceNow, Workday, GitHub Copilot, Databricks, cloud AI services, and governance controls. It should not be described as a separate AI budget or as a delivered financial outcome.

findings: Commercial terms are unevidenced for all seven confirmed vendors, including Epic, Microsoft, Tableau, SAS, AWS, and Databricks — blocking any contract-level sourcing or renewal analysis.
The outsourced analytics managed services provider controls SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS delivery; ~80% maintenance load leaves insufficient capacity for lakehouse or AI build.

findings: All seven use case value hypotheses are loaded but carry zero dollar amounts — no baseline spend, no realized savings, and no quantified opportunity is evidenced for any use case.
The lakehouse and AI/LLM governance hypotheses are foundational: their evidence gates must close before the remaining five use cases can produce any financial estimate.

profile.meaning: Meridian operates as both a clinical delivery system and a health plan, creating a dual data obligation — clinical EMR data from Epic and claims/financial data from the health plan side must eventually be unified.
profile.observed: 1 active profile row; high confidence; confirmed as planning-grade synthetic context.
profile.matters: The integrated payer-provider model means use cases like cost transparency and provider quality span organizational boundaries that are not yet bridged by a governed data layer.
profile.supports: All 7 use cases depend on this dual identity being resolved in a unified data model.

functions.meaning: All seven use cases have cross-functional executive sponsorship. The CEO, CFO, CIO, CTO, and CDAO are all aligned on the same use case portfolio, but each flags different evidence gaps as the primary blocker.
functions.observed: 6 active function rows; 217 candidate rows from executive interview alignment signals. 168 high-confidence, 55 medium-confidence.
functions.matters: Cross-functional alignment is a strategic asset. The risk is that without a shared governance model, each function will continue to operate its own data silo.
functions.supports: Use case prioritization and evidence closure accountability assignment.

org.meaning: Meridian's operating model is cross-functional: enterprise data, clinical operations, health plan operations, finance, quality, experience, and platform security all have a stake in the AI foundation.
org.observed: The ownership map shows CDAO-led data governance needs, CMO and health-plan operational demand, CFO value oversight, and CDIO platform/security dependencies.
org.matters: A McKinsey-style read would not start with tools; it would align decision rights first, because AI Agent Assist and lakehouse work cut across clinical, claims, finance, contact center, and platform teams.
org.supports: Supports executive alignment, governance workshop design, Moves phase gates, and owner-specific evidence asks.

workforce.meaning: The workforce layer captures how strategy, operating model, vendor, platform, and data concerns show up in executive interviews and role-level adoption risk.
workforce.observed: Interview-derived rows repeatedly point to maintenance-heavy analytics demand, unresolved governance, unclear ownership, and use-case teams waiting on the same data foundation prerequisites.
workforce.matters: AI Agent Assist is a work redesign, not a chatbot deployment. Agent workflows, analytics teams, clinical informatics, and contact-center operators all need evidence-backed changes to roles, controls, and adoption metrics.
workforce.supports: Supports change-impact framing, adoption risk review, workshop planning, and Moves evidence gates.

apps.meaning: Meridian's application landscape is a classic integrated health system pattern: a strong Epic clinical core surrounded by a fragmented analytics estate built on SQL Server marts, with multiple BI tools (Tableau, Power BI) creating duplicated metric definitions and ungoverned extract chains.
apps.observed: 12 active systems; 3 candidate (Tableau, CRM, Databricks). AWS and Databricks carry aspirational_not_ready lifecycle status.
apps.matters: The SQL Server mart sprawl is the primary technical debt blocking the lakehouse and governance use cases. The outsourced managed services provider consuming ~80% of capacity on maintaining this estate limits net-new delivery.
apps.supports: System-to-use-case dependency mapping and evidence closure sequencing.

data.meaning: Meridian has the raw data assets required for all seven use cases — clinical data in Epic, claims in the claims platform, pharmacy in the PBM, transcripts in the contact center, and financial data in the GL. The gap is not data existence but data governance: no certified harmonization, no identity spine, and no semantic layer.
data.observed: 17 active data asset rows; 220 candidate rows. High confidence on EMR, claims, pharmacy, STAR, FWA, billing patterns, and cost claims. Medium confidence on prior auth, CRM cases, provider attribution, and claims anomalies.
data.matters: The data exists but is siloed, ungoverned, and not harmonized. The lakehouse use case is the prerequisite for making this data usable across all other use cases.
data.supports: Evidence closure prioritization and data governance investment sequencing.

infra.meaning: The infrastructure layer separates current-state operating reality from future-state ambition, which is essential before recommending an AI or lakehouse roadmap.
infra.observed: The current analytics estate is fragmented and on-premise-heavy. AWS and Databricks appear as strategic targets, but the evidence still lacks certified landing zone, medallion, network/security, lineage, and operating controls.
infra.matters: For a CXO, this means the transformation is not to pick an AI use case first; it is to build the platform foundation that lets multiple clinical, financial, and member-experience use cases scale safely.
infra.supports: Supports architecture sequencing, platform readiness, cloud foundation planning, and evidence gates; blocks production lakehouse and production AI readiness claims.

vendors.meaning: Meridian's vendor portfolio reveals a two-tier dependency structure: a core clinical and analytics stack that is operational but ungoverned, and a target cloud layer that is aspirational and uncontracted for production use.
vendors.observed: Seven named vendors confirmed with high confidence — Epic, Microsoft, Tableau, SAS, an outsourced analytics managed services provider, AWS, and Databricks. Commercial terms are unevidenced for all seven. The managed services provider carries an ~80% maintenance load across SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS.
vendors.matters: The managed services contract structure directly limits Meridian's capacity to execute any of the seven use cases. Until contract scope and economics are evidenced, the CDAO cannot credibly plan net-new delivery against the AWS/Databricks target state.
vendors.supports: Supports vendor risk assessment and managed services contract review. Does not support sourcing decisions, commercial benchmarking, or platform build sequencing until contract terms and delivery capacity are evidenced.

budget.meaning: Meridian's IT budget and value dimension contains seven planning-grade value hypotheses — one per use case — but no baseline spend, no tower-level cost data, and no realized savings figures. Every value claim requires owner sign-off and evidence closure before it can be quantified.
budget.observed: Seven value hypotheses are loaded, each with a defined narrative and a consistent boundary: no dollar amounts, no realized value, and no baseline are evidenced. All seven carry the same constraint — value quantification requires certified evidence and finance/actuarial sign-off.
budget.matters: Without baseline spend and tower-level cost data, the CFO cannot prioritize investment sequencing, and Nexus cannot produce a business case for any of the seven use cases. The absence of financial baselines is the single largest barrier to moving from planning to decision grade.
budget.supports: Supports use case hypothesis framing and evidence gap identification. Does not support investment prioritization, ROI modeling, or sourcing-event outputs until FP&A validates baselines and tower owners sign off.

programs.meaning: Meridian's program portfolio maps 17 active data domain workstreams across the seven use cases, each with a defined system dependency chain and a specific set of evidence gates that must close before the program can advance.
programs.observed: Eleven program rows are confirmed across the lakehouse, AI/LLM, call center, and provider quality use cases. Every program row carries at least four unresolved evidence gates. The lakehouse programs depend on Epic Clarity, Claims, Pharmacy, and Databricks on AWS — none of which are certified for medallion-layer delivery.
programs.matters: The program portfolio confirms that Meridian's strategic intent is well-articulated but execution is blocked at the foundation layer. No program can advance to delivery without resolving the medallion architecture, identity spine, governance, and semantic layer gaps that are shared across all workstreams.
programs.supports: Supports program sequencing analysis and evidence gap prioritization. Does not support delivery commitments, milestone planning, or resource allocation until evidence gates are closed and program owners are confirmed.

ai.meaning: Meridian has enough context to prioritize AI investments, but not enough validated evidence to treat any use case as production-ready.
ai.observed: Every major AI use case depends on the same blockers: no certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no AI audit trail.
ai.matters: The boardroom decision is sequencing. The lakehouse and governance foundation should be treated as the enabling bet before scaling individual AI use cases.
ai.supports: Supports AI portfolio triage, sequencing, and evidence-backed investment framing; blocks production-readiness and quantified value claims.

risks.meaning: Meridian's risk and controls dimension surfaces 24 discrete, source-backed gap items mapped across all seven use cases. Every gap carries the same metric boundary: no value claim is permissible without a validated baseline. The risk profile is concentrated in four systemic gaps that affect every use case simultaneously.
risks.observed: Twelve risk rows are confirmed across the lakehouse, AI/LLM, and call center use cases, each with named affected systems, a metric boundary, and explicit forbidden claims. Four risks — no medallion architecture, no identity spine, no data governance, no semantic layer — appear across multiple use case clusters.
risks.matters: The concentration of systemic risks means that resolving the four pervasive blockers delivers disproportionate value: each closure unlocks multiple use cases simultaneously. Conversely, addressing use-case-specific risks in isolation — such as SAS lineage for payment integrity — will not unblock the broader portfolio.
risks.supports: Supports risk prioritization and evidence closure sequencing. Does not support risk mitigation claims, control certification, or audit readiness assertions — no controls are evidenced as operating effectively.

rel.meaning: The relationship layer is the guardrail that prevents Nexus from turning attractive AI ideas into unsupported implementation or value claims.
rel.observed: Unified clinical + claims repeatedly links Epic, claims, pharmacy, and Databricks target-state dependencies to medallion, identity, harmonization, and governance gaps.
rel.matters: A CXO needs to know which investment unlocks multiple outcomes. Here, the data foundation unlocks multiple use cases; isolated pilots would likely stall.
rel.supports: Supports cross-domain dependency reasoning, evidence-gap prioritization, and module handoffs once relationships are validated.

evidence.meaning: Meridian's evidence base is planning-grade and synthetic — it confirms system inventory, use case intent, and risk mapping with high confidence, but explicitly does not confirm production readiness, realized savings, or any certified architecture. The evidence layer is a structured claim boundary, not a proof of delivery.
evidence.observed: 500 source rows and 495 evidence references are loaded across seven use case bundles and eight explicit claim boundary records. All evidence is classified as synthetic_demo_phi_free_planning_grade. Eight boundary records explicitly prohibit specific claims — including production longitudinal patient views, implemented medallion architecture, and existing governance.
evidence.matters: The evidence architecture gives Meridian's leadership a clear and auditable map of what Nexus can and cannot assert. The eight explicit boundary records are not limitations to be resolved — they are the decision framework that defines which evidence must be collected from Meridian's own systems before any use case advances.
evidence.supports: Supports hypothesis framing, gap identification, and evidence collection prioritization. Does not support sourcing-event outputs, production readiness claims, or quantified value assertions — all of which require Meridian-sourced evidence with owner sign-off.

metrics.meaning: The metric layer protects the executive story from overclaiming by separating hypotheses, baselines, targets, and measured outcomes.
metrics.observed: Rows repeatedly mark baseline-required-before-value-claim across lakehouse, AI automation, call center, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and close automation.
metrics.matters: This is where Tower must eventually prove value. Until finance, clinical, and operational baselines are confirmed, the right answer is readiness and sequencing, not ROI.
metrics.supports: Supports baseline planning, Tower readiness, and value-governance design; blocks final value or savings claims.

industry.meaning: The industry lens turns generic healthcare trends into Meridian-specific implications: AI, quality, cost transparency, and member experience all depend on governed data.
industry.observed: Pattern rows repeatedly connect healthcare use cases to the same evidence gaps: medallion architecture, identity spine, transcript governance, contract terms, and semantic ownership.
industry.matters: This prevents a trend-led pitch. The story becomes: Meridian has the right use cases, but must prove the operating data foundation before scaling AI.
industry.supports: Supports executive positioning, peer-pattern framing, and prioritization; not benchmark claims or external market proof.

lenses.meaning: Seven expert lenses are loaded — one per use case — each mapping the industry pattern against Meridian's specific signal set. Six of seven are active; cost transparency is candidate status. All six active lenses confirm the same structural finding: Meridian's use case intent aligns with proven healthcare industry patterns, but every pattern requires foundational evidence that Meridian has not yet produced.
lenses.observed: All seven lenses carry high confidence except provider quality and performance, which is medium. Each lens surfaces four to five specific signals — all of which map directly to the 24 discrete risk and gap items in the risks dimension. No lens produces a recommendation that overrides a missing evidence gate.
lenses.matters: The expert lenses confirm that Meridian is pursuing the right use cases for an integrated health system and health plan of its profile. The strategic direction is sound. The constraint is not ambition — it is the absence of the foundational evidence required to execute against well-established industry patterns.
lenses.supports: Supports use case hypothesis validation and executive alignment on strategic direction. Does not override missing ownership, baseline, or platform proof — lens recommendations are advisory until Meridian-sourced evidence closes each gate.

ms.supports: Supports managed-services discovery, sourcing scope framing, and capacity-shift hypotheses; blocks vendor savings claims.

narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_title: Meridian Health System: Seven Use Cases, Zero Decision-Grade Outputs Without Evidence Closure
narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_summary:
Meridian operates as an integrated health system and health plan on Epic, with a fragmented on-prem analytics estate across SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS. An outsourced managed services provider consumes approximately 80% of analytics delivery capacity on maintenance, leaving minimal bandwidth for net-new work. AWS and Databricks are the stated target platform direction but are not production-ready, and no certified medallion architecture exists. Nexus has mapped 19 dimensions across 146 evidence references and 3,487 source rows, confirming system inventory, use case intent, and the risk landscape with high confidence.

Seven enterprise use cases are in scope — lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, call center optimization, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and automated close — and all remain in planning stage. Four pervasive blockers affect every use case simultaneously: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine. No use case can reach decision grade, and no value can be quantified, until these foundational gaps are closed. The immediate executive decision is sequencing: which evidence gates to close first, and who owns accountability for each.

quality_assessment.story_strength: The enterprise story is coherent and well-bounded: Meridian is an integrated payer-provider with a strong Epic clinical core, a fragmented on-prem analytics estate, and seven high-priority use cases that are all blocked by the same four foundational gaps (medallion architecture, data governance, semantic layer, identity spine). The narrative is honest about what Nexus can and cannot support, and the evidence gap structure gives executives a clear action agenda. The story would reach full McKinsey bar if baseline metrics (AHT, close cycle days, leakage rate) were loaded and value hypotheses could be bounded with directional ranges.
known_weaknesses: No baseline metrics loaded for any use case — AHT, close cycle, leakage rate, and HEDIS/STAR scores are all absent, preventing even directional value ranging.
Commercial contract terms are not evidenced for any vendor — total IT spend, vendor concentration risk, and renewal exposure cannot be assessed.
AWS and Databricks platform readiness is aspirational only — no network, security, IAM, or medallion architecture evidence exists, making the lakehouse timeline unassessable.
Finance and Actuarial function is candidate-status only — cost transparency and automated close use cases lack a confirmed finance owner.
Provider contract terms are in manual documents — digitization scope and timeline are unknown, blocking two use cases from advancing.
Workforce roles dimension has zero active rows — all 216 rows are candidate, meaning role-level accountability for evidence closure cannot be assigned.
quality_assessment.why_this_is_better_than_current: The current state at Meridian is a fragmented analytics estate with duplicated business rules, an outsourced managed services provider consuming ~80% of capacity on maintenance, and no shared governance model. Nexus provides the first integrated view of all 19 enterprise dimensions, maps the 24 specific evidence gaps blocking the 7 use cases, and gives the executive team a structured evidence closure agenda — replacing ad hoc stakeholder interviews with a governed, traceable context layer.
